NOTICE OF 128TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING
NOTICE is hereby given that the 128th Annual General Meeting (‘AGM’) of the Shareholders of the Company will be held on 
Wednesday, the 30th July, 2025 at 03:00 p.m. IST through Video Conferencing (‘VC’) / Other Audio-Visual Means (‘OAVM’) to 
transact the following business:
ORDINARY BUSINESS:

a) the Audited Standalone Financial Statements of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March, 2025 together 
with the Reports of the Board of Directors and Auditors thereon; and 
b) the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March, 2025 together 
with the Report of Auditors thereon.

NOTES FOR MEMBERS’ ATTENTION
1. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) has vide its General Circular no. 09/2024 dated 19th September, 2024 regarding 
“Clarification on holding of Annual General Meeting (AGM) through Video Conferencing (VC) or Other Audio Visual Means 
(OAVM)” along with other relevant General Circulars issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (‘MCA’) (hereinafter referred 
to as ‘MCA Circulars’) from time to time permitted the Companies whose AGMs are due in the year 2025, to conduct their 
AGMs up to 30th September, 2025 through VC/OAVM, without the physical presence of the members at a common venue 
and also provided relaxation from dispatching of physical copies of Notice of AGM and Financial Statements for year 
2025. Considering the above MCA Circulars, Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) vide its circular no. SEBI/
HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/133 dated 03rd October, 2024 in respect of “Relaxation from compliance with certain 
provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI Circular’) also provided 
relaxation up to 30th September, 2025 in this regard. In compliance with the MCA Circulars and SEBI Circular, the AGM of 
the members of the Company is being held through VC/OAVM. 
2. PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE ACT, A MEMBER ENTITLED TO ATTEND AND VOTE AT THE AGM IS ENTITLED TO 
APPOINT A PROXY TO ATTEND AND VOTE INSTEAD OF HIMSELF/HERSELF AND THE PROXY NEED NOT BE A MEMBER 
OF THE COMPANY.  
Since this AGM is being held pursuant to MCA Circulars and SEBI Circular through VC/OAVM, physical attendance of 
Members has been dispensed with. Accordingly, the facility for the appointment of proxies by the Members will not be 
available for the AGM and hence the Proxy Form, Attendance Slip and Route Map of AGM are not annexed to the Notice.
3. In accordance with the Secretarial Standard - 2 on General Meetings issued by the ICSI read with Clarification/Guidance 
on applicability of Secretarial Standards - 1 and 2 issued by the ICSI, the proceedings of the AGM through VC/OAVM shall 
be deemed to be conducted at the Registered Office of the Company at Century Bhavan, Dr. Annie Besant Road, Worli, 
Mumbai - 400 030. 
4. In compliance with the aforesaid MCA circulars and SEBI circular, Notice of the AGM along with Integrated Annual Report 
2024-25 is being sent only through electronic mode to those members whose email addresses are registered with the 
Company/Depositories. Members may note that the Notice of the AGM and the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 will 
also be available on the following websites:

THE INSTRUCTIONS FOR MEMBERS FOR REMOTE E-VOTING AND JOINING ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING ARE AS UNDER: -
I. In compliance with the provisions of Section 108 of the Act, Rule 20 of the Companies (Management and 
Administration) Rules, 2014 as amended from time to time, and Regulation 44 of the SEBI Listing Regulations and 
in terms of SEBI Circular no. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD/CIR/P/2020/242 dated 9th December, 2020, in relation to e-voting 
facility provided by listed entities, read with SEBI Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD2/CIR/P/2023/120 dated 11th 
July, 2023, in order to increase the efficiency of the voting process, it has been decided to enable e-voting to all the 
demat account holders, by way of a single login credential, through their demat accounts/websites of Depositories/
Depository Participants. The Company is pleased to provide to the members the facility to exercise their right to vote 
on resolutions proposed to be considered at the AGM, by electronic means and the business may be transacted 
through e-voting Services. For this purpose, the Company has entered into an agreement with National Securities 
Depository Limited (NSDL) for facilitating voting through electronic means, as the authorized agency. The facility of 
casting the votes by the members using an electronic voting system before the AGM (‘remote e-voting’) as well as 
e-voting on the date of AGM will be provided by NSDL.
II. The members who have cast their vote by remote e-voting prior to the AGM may also attend/participate in the AGM 
through VC/OAVM but shall not be entitled to cast their vote on such resolution again.
III. The remote e-voting period commences on Friday, 25th July, 2025 (09:00 a.m. IST) and ends on Tuesday, 29th July, 
2025 (05:00 p.m. IST). During this period, Members of the Company, holding shares either in physical form or in 
dematerialized form, as on the cut-off date i.e. Wednesday, 23rd July, 2025 , may cast their vote by remote e-voting. 
The remote e-voting module shall be disabled by NSDL for voting thereafter. Once the vote on a resolution is cast by 
the Member, the Member shall not be allowed to change it subsequently. Those Members, who will be present in the 
AGM through VC/OAVM facility and have not cast their vote on the Resolutions by remote e-voting and are otherwise 
not barred from doing so, shall be eligible to vote through e-voting system during the AGM.
IV. The facility of joining the AGM through VC/OAVM shall open 30 minutes before the time scheduled for the AGM 
and will be available for members on first-cum-first served basis and members can join by following the procedure 
mentioned in the Notice.

STEP 2: CAST YOUR VOTE ELECTRONICALL Y AND JOIN GENERAL MEETING ON NSDL E-VOTING SYSTEM:
How to cast your vote electronically and join General Meeting on NSDL e-voting system?
1. After successful login at Step 1, you will be able to see all the companies “EVEN” in which you are holding shares and 
whose voting cycle and General Meeting is in active status.
2. Select “EVEN” of Company for which you wish to cast your vote during the remote e-Voting period and casting your

Meeting”.
3. Now you are ready for e-voting as the voting page opens.
4. Cast your vote by selecting appropriate options i.e. assent or dissent, verify/modify the number of shares for which 
you wish to cast your vote and click on “Submit” and also “Confirm” when prompted.
5. Upon confirmation, the message “Vote cast successfully” will be displayed. 
6. You can also take the printout of the votes cast by you by clicking on the print option on the confirmation page.
7. Once you confirm your vote on the resolution, you will not be allowed to modify your vote.

Item No .7
With a view to restructure and create a focused, efficient, and strategically aligned business, the Company has made a pivotal 
portfolio choice to streamline its focus on its real estate business. It sees significant growth opportunities in the sector and is 
looking to drive sustained value creation for shareholders of the Company by becoming one of the leaders in this industry over 
time.  Aligned with that vision, the Company proposes to divest its Pulp and Paper undertaking via a sale and transfer of the 
same to ITC Limited ( “ITC” ) by way of a slump sale. This transaction is a vital step in the Company’s broader transformational 
growth phase, enabling it to generate and reallocate capital to its chosen focus area of real estate. 
Accordingly, the Board of Directors of the Company (“Board”) (which expression shall hereinafter also include a committee 
thereof) at their meeting held on March 31, 2025, and the Audit Committee of the Company, at their meeting held on  
March 31, 2025, subject to the approval of the members of the Company, receipt of regulatory approvals (and to conditions 
and modifications as may be prescribed or imposed by regulatory authorities while granting such approvals, which may be 
agreed to by the Board of Directors  and subject to such other conditions as the Board may agree)  and also subject to the 
fulfilment of various conditions, approved the execution of a Business Transfer Agreement ( “Business Transfer Agreement”) 
and other ancillary agreements (together, the “Definitive Agreements”) with ITC , for the sale and transfer of the Company’s 
Pulp and Paper Undertaking operated under the name of “Century Pulp and Paper”, as a going concern, on a slump sale basis, 
on such terms and conditions as detailed in the Business Transfer Agreement (including any amendments or modifications 
thereto) and all other agreements in connection therewith, for a lumpsum consideration of INR 3498,00,00,000 (Indian Rupees 
Three Thousand Four Hundred Ninety-Eight Crore), on a cash free and debt free basis, subject to closing and post-closing 
adjustments, in accordance with the terms of the Business Transfer Agreement (including any amendments or modifications 
thereto), in such manner and on such terms and conditions specified in the Definitive Agreements executed in relation to the 
transaction (such sale/ transfer/ hive off/ disposal of Undertaking from the Company to ITC be termed as the “Transaction”).

Aditya Birla Real Estate Limited1. Key Terms of the Transaction & Identification of the Undertaking:
• Execution Date: March 31, 2025
• Parties to the Business Transfer Agreement:  Aditya Birla Real Estate Limited (Seller) and ITC Limited (Buyer) 
• Undertaking:  The business of manufacture, distribution and sale of writing paper, printing paper, tissue paper, paper 
board, rayon grade pulp, paper grade pulp and other paper and paper-based products manufactured, sold and/
or distributed by the Company under the name of ‘Century Pulp & Paper’, including assets, inventory, contracts, 
licenses, intellectual property, employees, goodwill and liabilities and litigations pertaining to the Undertaking, except 
the assets and liabilities (including claims) that are specifically excluded in the Business Transfer Agreement. 
• Consideration:  INR 3,498 crores (Indian Rupees Three Thousand Four Hundred Ninety-Eight Crore), subject to 
customary closing and post-closing adjustments as per the Business Transfer Agreement.
• Conditions Precedent:  Completion of the Transaction is subject to satisfaction of certain conditions precedent agreed 
under the Business Transfer Agreement, including, receipt of (i) approval from the Government of Uttarakhand and 
the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India in order for ITC to get leasehold rights to the immovable 
property of the Company situated in LalKuan, Uttarakhand (ii) necessary regulatory approvals (including from the 
Competition Commission of India) and (iii) approvals from shareholders of the Company (under Section 180(1)(a) 
of the Companies Act, 2013 and Regulation 37A of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“LODR Regulations”), and other customary conditions. 
• Closing:  The Transaction will be consummated by the Parties upon completion of the conditions precedent specified 
in the Business Transfer Agreement. The Transaction was expected to be completed around 6 months from the 
Execution Date, as was communicated by the Company in the disclosure made to the stock exchanges under 
Regulation 30 of the LODR Regulations on March 31, 2025. This timeline is likely to be extended further in the event 
necessary approvals are not received within these timelines. 
• Non-solicit restrictions: ITC and the Company have agreed to customary non-solicit restrictions.  
• Non-compete restrictions: For a period of 4 (four) years post-Closing, the Company is not permitted to participate in 
any Competing Business (i.e., business in India of manufacture or distribution or sale of writing paper, printing paper, 
tissue paper, paper board, paper grade pulp or any other paper and paper based products being manufactured or sold 
or supplied by the Company as on the execution date or the closing date) subject to customary exceptions. 
• License of the Century Mark: In connection with the consummation of the Transaction, the Company also proposes 
to enter into a license agreement with ITC for providing ITC a limited license to use the ‘Century’ Mark (i.e., “Century” 
brands or logos, including the “C” Device, whether used alone or in any combination of words or figures along with 
the “Century” brand or logo) for a period of 12 (twelve) months from the date of Closing in respect of specified 
products, to facilitate a smooth transition of marketing and sales aspects of the Undertaking from the Company to 
ITC. Further, as part of the Transaction, the Company has agreed not to use, assign, or license the Century Mark for 
any Competing Business for 20 (twenty) years. 
• Ancillary Agreements: The Company and ITC will also enter into certain agreements in furtherance of the Business 
Transfer Agreement with effect from the date of Closing, including the following: 
(i) Transition Services Agreement, for provision of certain services by the Company to the Buyer, for provision of 
mutually agreed services by the Company to ITC, for a period of 12 (twelve) months or such other mutually 
agreed period;
(ii) Plant Conveyance Deed, for the sale, transfer and conveyance of the Plant from the Company to the Buyer;
(iii) IP Assignment Deed, recording terms and conditions with respect to the perpetual transfer of rights of the 
Company in the Undertaking IP to the Buyer; and
(iv) Century License Agreement (as specified above).
• Other Key Terms: The Business Transfer Agreement also contains customary representations, warranties, 
indemnities, other customary covenants, and pre-closing and post-closing obligations.

Aditya Birla Real Estate Limited2. Need/ Justification/ Rationale for the Transaction:
The Transaction is intended to streamline the Company’s business, thereby allowing it to focus on the real estate business. 
The divestment of the Pulp and Paper undertaking is a value unlocking exercise for the Company. It will further enable the 
Company to pursue growth opportunities in its core business – i.e., real estate. The aforesaid sale creates a more focused, 
efficient, and strategically aligned company and would unlock value for the shareholders of the Company. 
3. Valuation of the Undertaking:
The Company, along with its exclusive financial advisor, had initiated a process for exploring bidders for the sale of the pulp 
and paper business. The Company received initial non-binding bids from multiple parties, post which it shortlisted a few 
parties for further discussions wherein ITC emerged as the highest and most credible bidder. Considering negotiations 
and potential economies of scale for its paperboards and specialty papers business, ITC was agreed upon as the Buyer 
for the pulp and paper undertaking.
In its public disclosure to the stock exchanges dated 31 March 2025, ITC noted that: 
“The acquisition will immediately add significant scale and economies to existing operations with potential for further 
capacity expansion, provide locational advantage for efficient customer servicing and proximity to key raw material 
sources, mitigate operational risks through multi-site operations and enhance resilience across industry cycles through 
portfolio diversification.”     
The Consideration for the Transaction is INR 3,498 crores (Indian Rupees Three Thousand Four Hundred Ninety-Eight Crore), 
(subject to customary closing and post-closing adjustments as per the Business Transfer Agreement). The Consideration 
for the Transaction has been determined, pursuant to among others, a Valuation Report dated 29th March, 2025, issued by 
Bansi Mehta & Co. Chartered Accountants (“Valuation Report”), an independent valuer appointed by the Company. 
4. Details of the Buyer/ Relationship with the Promoters:
The Buyer is ITC Limited, a public limited company incorporated under the laws of India, bearing Corporate Identity Number 
(CIN): L16005WB1910PLC001985 and having its registered office at Virginia House, 37 Jawaharlal Nehru Road, Kolkata, 
West Bengal - 700 071. The equity shares of ITC are listed on the BSE Ltd., the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. and

6. Use of Consideration received pursuant to the Transaction:
The Company plans to strategically deploy the Consideration received from this transaction to primarily reduce its 
outstanding debt, thereby strengthening its balance sheet and improving financial flexibility to fuel future growth. The 
Company expects to repay around INR 2000,00,00,000 (Indian Rupees Two Thousand Crores) of debt relating to the pulp 
and paper undertaking. A significant portion of the balance funds will be deployed towards real estate, including allocation 
towards acquiring additional land parcels, which is crucial for expanding its core real estate business and pursuing new 
development opportunities.

None of the directors, key managerial personnel of the Company or any of their relatives (as defined in the Companies 
Act, 2013) are concerned or interested (financially or otherwise) in this Transaction, except to the extent of their respective 
shareholding (if any) in the Company and in ITC. 
8. Requirement of Shareholders’ Approval:
In terms of Section 180(1)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013 approval of the shareholders is required by way of a special 
resolution to sell, dispose off or otherwise transfer the whole or substantially the whole of any undertaking in which 
the investment of the company, exceeds 20% (twenty per cent) of its net worth as per the audited balance sheet of the 
preceding financial year or an undertaking which generates 20% (twenty per cent) of the total income of the company 
during the previous financial year. Since the net-worth of the Undertaking exceeds 20% (twenty per cent) of the net-worth 
of the Company in FY 2024-25 and also income of the Undertaking exceeds 20% (twenty per cent) of the total income of 
the Company in FY 2024-25 and accordingly, the Transaction is required to be approved by members of the Company by 
way of a special resolution, in terms of Section 180(1)(a) of the Companies Act. Additionally, in compliance with Regulation 
37A of the LODR Regulations, a special resolution shall only be acted upon only if the votes cast by the public shareholders 
in favour of the resolution exceed the votes cast by such public shareholders against the resolution provided that no public 
shareholder shall vote on the resolution if he is a party, directly or indirectly, to the Transaction.
9. Audit Committee and Board Approval:
The Audit Committee of the Company, at its meeting held on March 31, 2025, took note of the Valuation Report placed 
before it and recommended the Transaction to the Board.
The Board took note of the Business Transfer Agreement and related documents and were satisfied that the Consideration 
payable in respect of the Transaction is fair and reasonable and that the Transaction in the best interests of the Company 
and its stakeholders. The Board accordingly recommends Item No. 7 for approval by way of a Special Resolution with 
majority of public shareholders casting their vote in favour. 
None of the Directors or Key managerial personnel of the Company or their relatives are, in any way, concerned or

Regulation 23(4) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, (‘SEBI Listing Regulations’), 
as amended, mandates approval of Members by means of an Ordinary Resolution, in case of any ‘Material Related Party 
Transaction’ (i.e., a transaction with a Related Party shall be considered material, if the transaction(s) to be entered into 
individually or taken together with previous transactions during a financial year exceeds Rs. 1,000 Crore or 10% of annual 
consolidated turnover of the Company as per the last audited financial statements of the Company, whichever is lower).  
=== page 24 ===
23
Aditya Birla Real Estate LimitedRegulation 2(1)(zc) of SEBI Listing Regulations defines “related party transaction” means a transaction involving a transfer 
of resources, services or obligations between: (i) a listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on one hand and a related party of 
the listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on the other hand; or (ii) a listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on one hand, and 
any other person or entity on the other hand, the purpose and effect of which is to benefit a related party of the listed entity 
or any of its subsidiaries, with effect from April 1, 2023; regardless of whether a price is charged and a “transaction” with 
a related party shall be construed to include a single transaction or a group of transactions in a contract.
In accordance with the above context, the Resolution No. 8 is proposed for the approval of the Members of the Company.
Both the related parties viz. Birla Estates Private Limited (BEPL), a Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company and Vardhita 
Properties Private Limited (VPPL), a joint venture of BEPL, are engaged in the business of real estate development. BEPL 
owns a land parcel situated at Sarjapur, Bengaluru, and has entered into a joint venture arrangement with global investor, 
Mitsubishi Estate Co. Ltd. (MECL) through its affiliate MJR Investment Pte Ltd. (MIPL) for residential housing development 
through VPPL.
Since the said land parcel is being developed by VPPL under the project ‘Birla Evara’, VPPL is in the process of availing 
term loan i.e. project finance up to Rs.500 crores in one or more tranches from the Bank(s)/Financial Institution(s) to fund 
the working capital / construction finance requirement of the said project. In order to avail the borrowing facility, BEPL 
is required to mortgage the project land at Sarjapur, Bengaluru in favour of the Bank(s)/Financial Institution(s)/Security 
Trustee(s) as the land ownership is with BEPL and the development rights for this land is with VPPL.
The proposed related party transaction pertaining to creation of mortgage of land by BEPL in favor of the the Bank(s)/
Financial Institution(s)/Security Trustee(s) for the benefit and on behalf of VPPL to secure the borrowings by VPPL up 
to Rs. 500 crores, in one or more tranches, and interest thereon, exceed the materiality threshold of 10% of the annual 
consolidated turnover (i.e. Rs.4,392 crores) of the Company as per the last audited financial statements for the year ended 
31st March, 2025, being a material related party transaction and therefore, requires prior approval of the Audit Committee 
and Members of  the Company in terms of Regulation 23 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The proposed transaction is in 
the ordinary course of business.

About the Report
Purpose of the Report
The Integrated Annual Report FY 2024–25 
(hereinafter referred to as ‘the Report’) builds 
upon the previous fiscal year’s Report, aligning 
key sustainability issues of ABREL’s with the 
relevant sections of the Report. It visually 
represents the Company’s value creation 
journey in the context of its long-term vision. 
This report goes beyond financial disclosures 
by integrating both financial and non-financial 
performance data, demonstrating how ABREL 
generates sustainable value across short, 
medium, and long-term horizons.
By aligning key environmental, social, and 
governance (ESG) aspects with strategic 
priorities, the Report provides insights into 
business opportunities, risks, and stakeholder 
relationships. The goal is to foster transparency, 
accountability, and trust among key 
stakeholders, including investors, customers, 
employees, regulators, and communities.
Reporting Standards and 
Frameworks
The Integrated Annual Report for the financial 
year 2024–25 has been carefully developed in 
line with the International Integrated Reporting 
Framework, as established by the International 
Financial Reporting Standards Foundation 
(IFRS). To provide a thorough representation of 
the Company’s performance, this report also 
adheres to the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) 
Standards 2021 and aligns ABREL’s efforts with 
United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 
(UN SDGs). Additionally, the financial and 
statutory information in this report complies 
with the requirements of the Companies Act, 
2013, along with its associated rules and the Indian Accounting Standards. The Company 
has also ensured full compliance with the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and 
Secretarial Standards. Furthermore, this report 
includes the Business Responsibility and 
Sustainability Report (BRSR) for the financial 
year 2024–25, offering a transparent and 
holistic overview of ABREL’s operations and 
impacts.
Reporting Scope and 
Boundaries
This report covers the time period from 
1st April, 2024, to 31st March, 2025. It 
includes both financial and non-financial 
information shared by the Company. This 
report gives a detailed overview of ABREL’s 
operations, including its key business 
segments like Real Estate (Birla Estates) and 
Pulp & Paper.
The reporting scope this year includes 
updates from project sites in the Mumbai 
Metropolitan Region (Maharashtra), Bengaluru 
(Karnataka), National Capital Region 
(Delhi-NCR), Pune, and the manufacturing 
facility in Lalkuan (Uttarakhand).
The Report focusses on important topics that 
impact ABREL’s operations and are relevant to 
its stakeholders, including value chain 
partners, customers, and communities, 
among others. As part of its commitment to 
transparency, the Company continues to 
share annual updates on its Environmental, 
Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives, 
following the International Integrated 
Reporting Framework. Relevant historical 
trends are included, and any exclusions are 
clearly disclosed.ABREL publishes this report annually and 
shares financial results every quarter. For more 
information, please contact Mr. Shailendra 
Joshi at abrel.info@adityabirla.com  
or call +91 22 2495 7000.
Materiality
ABREL assesses materiality from the viewpoint 
of strategic relevance and long-term value 
creation. The key issues, opportunities, and 
challenges that significantly affect the 
Company’s business and its capacity to deliver 
value to stakeholders are central to its 
Integrated Report. 
By applying clear materiality criteria, the 
Company identifies the most relevant topics for 
its stakeholders. To determine and prioritise the 
material topics that influence stakeholders, 
strategy, and value creation, the Company 
gathers feedback from various business units 
and key stakeholders. This process includes 
detailed surveys, in-depth discussions with 
internal and external parties, scoring each 
topic, and developing a materiality matrix.
In the current fiscal year, the Company has 
conducted a comprehensive review of its 
materiality assessment. ABREL has re-evaluated 
the key material topics, building on the 
Stakeholder Engagement and Materiality 
Assessment (SEMA) conducted in  
FY 2023–24. This includes reviewing peer 
company reports and industry standards 
relevant to its Real Estate and Pulp & Paper 
segments. For more information refer to the 
Materiality Assessment section of the Report.

India in FY  2024–25: Standing 
Strong  in a Fractured World
India emerged as an outlier of stability and 
momentum in a world adrift. With projected 
GDP growth of 6.4–6.5%, it retained 
its crown as the fastest-growing major 
economy. The final quarter surged to 7.4%, 
powered by construction, manufacturing, 
and sustained government capital outlay.Policy credibility, macroeconomic 
resilience, and diversified growth 
engines underpinned this performance. 
Consumption rebounded and exports rose. 
Agriculture benefited from favourable 
monsoons and strong foodgrain output. 
Services, still India’s growth mainstay, grew 
by 7.2%, accounting for over half of gross 
value added.
India’s export story was particularly telling. 
Merchandise and services exports reached 
an all-time high of US$ 824.9 billion, up 
6.01% year-on-year, a feat few economies 
could match amid global headwinds.
Inflation, a lingering concern globally, 
trended down decisively. The headline 
rate eased to 4.6%, from 5.4% a year 
earlier, helped by effective supply-side 
interventions, softening input costs, and 
timely monetary policy adjustments. 
The Reserve Bank of India moved from 
tightening to a neutral stance in October 
2024, then back to accommodative in 
April 2025.
The financial system stood firm. Balance 
sheets strengthened and asset quality 
improved. Loan growth remained in double 
digits. Yields softened across government 
and corporate debt, reinforcing investor 
confidence.
India enters the new fiscal year with 
tailwinds intact. GDP growth is projected 
at 6.5%, with risks well-balanced. 
Consumption is expected to pick up further. 
Public investment will likely remain a key 
growth lever, while fiscal consolidation 
continues.
Manufacturing momentum is expected to 
build, supported by the Production Linked

Geopolitical tensions, now more durable

Your Company’s Performance
Your Company, Aditya Birla Real Estate Ltd. 
(formerly Century Textiles and Industries 
Limited) has embarked on a transformative 
journey to establish itself as one of India’s 
foremost real estate players. FY 2024–25 
marked a pivotal year in this evolution. The 
Company restructured its portfolio, delivering 
exceptional growth in its core real estate 
business. The Board approved the divestment 
of its Pulp & Paper division—sharpening 
both balance sheet and management focus 
on real estate, with a view to long-term value 
creation. This transaction, structured as a 
slump sale to ITC under a Business Transfer 
Agreement, is valued at ` 3,498 crore, 
subject to certain conditions precedent. 
Completion is expected by Q2 FY25.
India’s real estate sector continues to 
exhibit resilience and steady expansion, 
supported by macroeconomic stability, 
accelerating urbanisation, and evolving 
lifestyle aspirations. Projects with the right 
location and a trusted brand are seeing 
robust traction. Birla Estates, a wholly owned 
subsidiary of Aditya Birla Real Estate Limited 
and the Group’s flagship real estate vehicle, 
is currently developing a residential portfolio 
of approximately 35 million sq. ft., with an 
estimated gross development value (GDV) 
of ` 70,000 crore. This includes presales 
of ` 17,253 crore. Strategically focused on 
four key markets—Mumbai Metropolitan 
Region (MMR), Bengaluru, National Capital 
Region (NCR), and Pune—the Company is

Circular Economy and Waste 
Management

repurposed, or recovered rather than 
discarded. Circularity has been integrated 
across our operations. In the Real Estate

Business Verticals
ABREL thrives through its diverse business segments, including Real Estate and Pulp & Paper. In Real Estate, the Company creates spaces that inspire 
and endure, going beyond mere structures. The Pulp & Paper division is dedicated to sustainable practices, manufacturing materials that set new 
standards for environmental responsibility. Together, these varied segments highlight ABREL’s adaptability and resilience. They position the Company 
as a dynamic entity capable of meeting the diverse demands of different industries while upholding a strong commitment to excellence.
Real Estate 
Birla Estates Private Limited (‘Birla 
Estates’ or ‘BEPL’), a wholly owned 
subsidiary of ABREL is the real estate 
venture of the Aditya Birla Group. In 
2016, Birla Estates was established with 
the philosophy of LIFEDESIGNED® 
home and office spaces. BEPL’s mission 
is to transform the Indian Real Estate 
sector by creating value and providing 
an unparalleled experience for all 
stakeholders. In a short span, BEPL 
has positioned itself as a trusted and 
premium real estate brand, delivering 
high-quality residential and commercial 
developments across key urban markets 
including MMR, Bengaluru, Delhi-NCR, 
and Pune. It is actively expanding its footprint across India and seeks to foster 
strategic partnerships across the value 
chain to ensure timely delivery, quality 
construction, and innovation.
Birla Estates adopts a balanced growth 
strategy, developing land through outright 
acquisitions, asset-light joint ventures, 
and leveraging its own land bank. It aims 
to become one of the top real estate 
companies in India by focussing on 
customer-centricity, sustainability, execution 
excellence, and innovative design.
The Company’s residential projects are 
thoughtfully planned to enhance urban 
living with integrated green spaces, 
wellness features, and lifestyle amenities. Landmark projects such as Birla Niyaara 
in Mumbai exemplify its premium 
offerings. On the commercial front, 
Birla Estates owns and operates two 
Grade A office buildings in Worli, 
Mumbai, offering approximately 6.1 
lakhs Sq. Ft. of leasable area, designed 
to ensure business efficiency and 
employee well-being.
As part of ABREL and backed by the 
legacy of the Aditya Birla Group, 
Birla Estates is well-positioned to lead 
the next phase of growth in Indian 
real estate. It aims to create modern, 
inclusive, and sustainable urban spaces 
for future generations.

Pulp & Paper
Located in the scenic region of 
Lalkuan, Uttarakhand, the Pulp & Paper 
segment, Century Pulp & Paper, is a 
leading industry figure. Since 1984, 
this division has been recognised for 
producing premium writing and printing 
paper, packaging board, green pulp,

manufacturer of paper, board, tissue, 
and pulp from a single location in India, the Company has also made a significant 
mark in the global export market. With 
service centres and sales offices worldwide, 
the division ensures a seamless experience 
for customers.

environmental impact across its operations.

participates in community development 
initiatives, reflecting its dedication to the 
welfare of the communities it serves. ABREL’s 
consistent focus on quality, sustainability, 
and social engagement continues to set high 
standards within the industry.

Risk Management
ABREL regards risk management as more 
than a compliance requirement. It serves 
as a critical enabler of strategic resilience 
and sustainable value creation. The 
Company’s Enterprise Risk Management 
(ERM) framework is designed to proactively 
identify, assess, and mitigate risks across 
all levels of the organisation, aligning risk 
oversight with the Company’s long-term 
strategic objectives.
Guided by best practices, ABREL’s ERM 
approach integrates risk governance 
into decision-making processes across 
functions and business segments. The Risk 
Management Committee of the Board, 
supported by the Board of Directors, plays a 
key role in defining the overall risk appetite, 
approving risk policies, and overseeing the 
effectiveness of the ERM system.The Central Risk Office, operating under 
the leadership of the Chief Financial 
Officer (CFO), coordinates enterprise-wide 
risk identification and mitigation efforts. 
It collaborates closely with functional and 
business unit heads to ensure the continuous 
monitoring of strategic, operational, 
environmental, reputational, regulatory, or 
climate-related risks. It also ensures the timely 
escalation of critical issues through structured 
reporting mechanisms.
Each business segment owns its risk profile. 
Business functions remain accountable 
for identifying potential threats, assessing 
likelihood and impact, and implementing 
mitigation plans. These risk insights are 
regularly reviewed at both Management 
and Board levels to ensure agility and 
preparedness in an increasingly dynamic 
operating environment.To increase risk intelligence, the Company 
is adopting technology-driven tools for risk 
visualisation, heat mapping, and predictive 
analytics. This data-driven approach proves 
essential as the Company navigates risks 
associated with climate change, regulatory 
transitions, market trends, and stakeholder 
expectations.
ABREL’s dedication to a solid risk culture, 
continuous training, and transparent 
communication embeds risk awareness at 
every organisational level. This proactive 
and integrated risk management approach 
helps the Company protect value while 
unlocking new opportunities in a rapidly 
evolving business space.

consistently across all business divisions

timely and accurate tax settlements.
Given the ever-changing regulatory

Enhancing Energy Efficiency with Low-E Glass at Birla Niyaara
The Real Estate division integrates 
Low-Emissivity (Low-E) glass into project 
façades to meet stringent sustainability, 
thermal comfort, and visual performance 
goals. This material choice aligns with the 
organisation’s NCA and LifeDesigned® 
philosophies, which aim to create high-
performance built environments that 
promote energy efficiency and occupant 
well-being.Why Low-E Glass?
Low-E glass was selected for its balanced 
performance in energy efficiency, indoor 
comfort, and design clarity.
 Thermal Insulation: 
 Limits solar heat gain and heat loss, 
reducing dependency on artificial 
cooling and heating.
 Daylight Harvesting:
 Admits visible light while blocking 
infrared radiation, enhancing 
occupant well-being and lowering 
lighting energy consumption.
 UV Protection:
 Blocks up to 99% of UV radiation, 
minimising material fading and health 
risks.
 Condensation Control:
 Maintains stable surface 
temperatures, reducing mould growth 
and maintenance needs.
 Design Consistency: 
 Provides optical clarity, tint options, 
and clean architectural lines 
compatible with premium façades.Implementation

For example, at Birla Niyaara, maturity 
sensors were deployed in concrete to non-
destructively assess in-place strength. This 
real-time monitoring enhanced precision 
in construction timelines, improved 
quality control, and enabled data-driven 
optimisation of concrete mixes, thereby 
reducing material wastage and resource 
consumption.In addition, the Company developed and 
implemented a Sustainable Procurement 
Plan for Birla Niyaara, aligned with BREEAM 
standards. The plan encourages the use 
of responsibly sourced materials (e.g., 
FSC-certified wood), prioritises local 
sourcing within a 400 km radius, and 
supports lifecycle-based product selection. 
Collectively, these efforts ensure that 
sustainability is embedded into the DNA of the Company’s design from intent to 
execution.
Each of ABREL’s developments is

harmonising thoughtful design with climate

architectural intent.

Quality: Embedding Rigour into 
Every Detail
Quality at the Company is not treated as a 
checklist; it functions as a deeply held value 
that guides each phase of work, from early-
stage planning through to final handover. 
In FY 2024–25, this principle was formally 
embedded through the rollout of a 
comprehensive Quality Management System 
(QMS), aligned with the ISO 9001:2015 
standard. The system includes uniform 
quality management plans, approved 
specifications for materials, inspection 
and testing protocols, and performance 
benchmarks consistently across all projects.
This structured system is supported by 
real-time assessment tools and a culture 
of continuous site-level innovation. One 
such initiative involved the deployment 
of wireless maturity sensors that measure in-place concrete strength without damage. 
These ASTM C1074-compliant devices 
continuously record temperature, hydration 
history, and compressive strength, allowing 
for more informed decisions around 
the timing of formwork removal and 
construction cycles. Their use has helped 
improve quality consistency while optimising 
construction timelines and resource 
deployment.
On-the-ground innovations also played a key 
role in addressing persistent construction 
challenges. In areas prone to seepage 
and shrinkage, the Company introduced 
fog-based curing methods, combined 
thermocol and sand insulation in deep raft 
foundations, and adopted temperature-
controlled concrete (TCC) protocols to 
ensure proper curing. To address water 
ingress from wet-to-dry area transitions, 
measures such as micro-concrete bands at balcony and toilet junctions, and damp-
proof course (DPC) layers under partition 
walls were implemented to block capillary 
rise.
The Company’s quality-led approach was 
formally recognised when Birla Estates 
received the Golden Peacock National 
Quality Award 2025, presented by the 
Institute of Directors, India. As the only 
real estate firm to receive the honour in 
the quality category this year, the award, 
selected from over 400 applicants across 
sectors, validated the Company’s sustained 
focus on refined, resilient, and robust 
construction practices.
Together, these initiatives underscore a 
core belief: that true customer value begins 
with a commitment to quality thoughtfully 
embedded into every detail, from structural 
frameworks to finishing elements.
To improve construction quality, minimise 
delays, and enhance structural reliability, 
Birla Estates has implemented wireless 
concrete maturity sensors at select sites 
during FY 2024–25. This approach 
replaces traditional cube and cylinder 
testing methods with a non-destructive, 
real-time system that adheres to the ASTM 
C1074 standard. The initiative reflects 
Birla Estates’ broader commitment 
to quality excellence as part of its 
LifeDesigned® philosophy.
Why It Matters
Traditional methods for testing concrete 
compressive strength depend on cast 
samples, which are labour-intensive, 
time-sensitive, and frequently do not 
reflect actual in-place conditions. Maturity 
sensors provide a more accurate, 
efficient, and real-time solution by 
tracking the temperature history of the 
concrete, which directly correlates with 
its strength development.System Specifications and 
Methodology
 Standard followed: 
 ASTM C1074 – Maturity method for 
estimating concrete strength
 Device used:
 InSite RPX loggers, which can 
continuously monitor temperature and 
strength for up to 180 days
 Data capture frequency:
 Every 60 seconds
 Monitoring range: 
 –20°C to 125°C
 Cloud integration: 
 Sensor data is uploaded using mobile 
readers and synchronised with the 
InSite cloud platform, allowing easy 
access at the site level

Pulp & Paper: Sustaining Excellence in 
Manufacturing
In FY 2024–25, the Pulp & Paper division 
delivered a robust production output of 
447,508 MT, reflecting the Company’s 
commitment to operational excellence, 
product innovation, and responsible 
manufacturing. Driven by the principles 
of World Class Manufacturing (WCM) 
and sustainability-focussed initiatives, the 
division strengthened productivity, optimised 
resource utilisation, and introduced 
innovative, market-relevant products aligned 
with evolving customer needs.
A culture of continuous improvement is 
deeply embedded in operations, with over 
1,200 Kaizen suggestions successfully 
implemented during the year. These initiatives 
led to tangible outcomes, including reduced 
fibre loss, enhanced water efficiency, 
significant energy savings, and improved 
product quality across manufacturing plants.
With strategic investments in cutting-edge 
R&D, the division expanded its portfolio 
of sustainable and value-added products, 
while maintaining a strong focus on cost 
efficiency and environmental responsibility. 
Collectively, these efforts position the Pulp & 
Paper division as a leader in delivering both 
economic value and long-term sustainable 
growth.
Focus Area
The Pulp & Paper division of ABREL operates 
under five strategic pillars: Maximisation 
of Forest Value through Sustainable Forest 
Management, Commitment to Superior 
Quality Standards, Continuous Improvement 
in Manufacturing Processes, Utilisation of 
Renewable Energy Resources in Industrial 
Operations, and Impact-Oriented Society 
through Recycling. These core focus areas 
collectively support the division’s mission 
to achieve operational excellence, drive 
responsible innovation, and advance circular 
economy principles throughout the value 
chain.Maximising Forest Value 
through Sustainable Forest 
Management
Sustainable forest management is central 
to the raw material sourcing strategy of 
ABREL’S Pulp & Paper division. With a 
clear understanding that long-term business 
resilience is directly linked to ecosystem 
health, the division continues to implement 
structured, impact-driven initiatives that 
balance economic growth with environmental 
preservation. The goal is not only to fulfil 
the raw material needs for high-quality 
paper production but also to contribute 
meaningfully to India’s green cover and the 
enhancement of rural livelihoods.
In FY 2024–25, ABREL expanded its 
flagship Social Forestry Programme, enabling 
sustainable sourcing while enhancing 
community welfare. Over 1.11 Crore saplings 
were planted across more than 5,000 
hectares of land, significantly contributing 
to carbon sequestration and biodiversity 
enhancement. These initiatives were carried 
out in close collaboration with local farming 
communities, providing technical guidance 
on sustainable agroforestry practices and 
offering a dependable income stream 
through long-term buyback arrangements.
ABREL focusses on cultivating fast-growing 
species such as eucalyptus and bamboo, 
known for their high carbon absorption 
capacity and short harvest cycles, ensuring 
sustainable yields without causing long-term 
environmental degradation. By prioritising 
plantations over natural forest sourcing, 
the Company reduces pressure on critical 
ecosystems and aids in conserving 
biodiversity hotspots.These sustainable forestry efforts are also 
integral to ABREL’s broader decarbonisation 
strategy. Large-scale plantation drives 
directly contribute to carbon sequestration 
and align with the Aditya Birla Group’s Net 
Zero ambitions. Beyond environmental 
impacts, these initiatives have delivered 
substantial socioeconomic benefits, creating 
employment and supporting livelihoods in 
rural communities, particularly for women 
and marginal farmers.
ABREL actively monitors and manages its 
raw material supply chains through stringent 
sustainability standards, including compliance 
with FSC® (Forest Stewardship Council) 
certification requirements for responsible 
forest management. The Company’s 
procurement strategies emphasise local 
sourcing wherever feasible, promoting rural 
livelihoods, while minimising transportation-
related emissions.
Through these holistic measures, ABREL 
continues to build a responsible and resilient 
value chain, one that secures raw material 
availability, safeguards natural ecosystems, 
and uplifts the communities that sustain them.
Driving Circular Economy 
through Recycling and 
Waste Management
The Pulp & Paper division of ABREL places 
strong emphasis on fostering a circular 
economy by optimising raw material 
utilisation and integrating robust recycling 
practices throughout its operations. This 
approach not only enhances material 
efficiency but also significantly reduces the 
Company’s environmental footprint.

Key Initiatives and Outcomes in FY 2024–25
Circular Use of Production-Related Waste
At the Pulp & Paper division, ABREL achieved a near 100% waste diversion rate from landfill through effective recycling and reuse 
practices. Of the total waste generated, 99.58%, comprising primarily hazardous waste such as ETP and DIP sludge, along with non-
hazardous waste such as fly ash, dry pith, wet pith, wood bark, wood dust and bagasse waste, is managed directly within production 
activities. This approach minimises waste disposal and contributes to resource circularity.
Construction and Packaging Waste Reduction
The softwood content in board production has been reduced from 15% to 10% in the top layer and from 10% to 5% in the back 
layer, resulting in annual savings. Additionally, the thickness of plastic film has been decreased from 65 microns to 50 microns, 
leading to further savings and a reduction in plastic consumption.Effluent Water Reuse and Water Loop Closures
Closed water loops at unbleached thickeners across multiple plants in the Pulp & Paper division have led to substantial reductions 
in effluent colour and discharge volumes. At PM3, the reuse of soft water resulted in a daily reduction of 1,000 m³ in freshwater 
consumption.
Waste-to-Value Initiatives
Rejects from machine centricleaners are now reprocessed through the DIP (De-Inking Plant), resulting in a 0.5% improvement in DIP 
yield. Additionally, coating materials recovered from service tanks are redirected to recovery tanks, thereby reducing the load on 
ETP systems.
Through these initiatives, ABREL continues to advance its journey towards a zero-waste future by transforming operational waste streams into valuable 
resources and strengthening its commitment to sustainable production.Productivity and Cost Efficiencies through Raw Material Optimisation
The Company reduced softwood usage from 15% to 10% in the top layer and from 10% to 5% in the back layer of board products, 
leading to production cost savings. Additionally, the replacement of 65-micron films with 50-micron films in packaging decreased 
plastic consumption and contributed to further cost savings.
Responsible Hazardous Waste Handling
Hazardous wastes such as used oil, sludge, and chemical residues, are thoroughly tracked and disposed of by authorised recyclers 
and incinerators in accordance with CPCB EPR guidelines, ensuring 100% compliance with environmental regulations.
Energy Recovery and Black Liquor Management
In the bagasse pulp mill, modifications to the black liquor line have improved washing processes and reduced soda loss, thereby 
improving recovery efficiency. Bio-methanation systems continue to convert bagasse wastewater into methane, contributing to clean 
energy generation.

Continuous Improvement in Manufacturing Processes
Utilising Renewable Energy Resources in Industrial Operations
ABREL’s Pulp & Paper division continues to strengthen its commitment to a clean energy transition. During the year, the focus remained on increasing 
the use of renewable energy across operations and reducing dependence on fossil fuels.At ABREL’s Pulp & Paper division, operational excellence is driven by a relentless focus on process innovation and resource optimisation. Guided 
by the principles of World Class Manufacturing (WCM), the Company continues to streamline operations, improve productivity, and enhance cost 
efficiency through targeted upgrades and process improvements.

Efficiency
  A new-generation headbox was installed

repulp rejections.
 At PM2, rewinder upgrades, including

eliminated bobbin generation, enhancing 
workplace safety and reducing workforce 
deployment.

breaks.2Energy and Resource

its commitment to responsible water

 Installation of two-stage pressure screens 
in PGP improved pulp cleanliness and 
reduced fibre loss.

methanation plant during FY 2024–25. 
This facility exemplifies the principles 
of circular economy by converting 
high-Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) 
wastewater from bagasse-based pulp 
processing into a valuable renewable 
energy source—Compressed Methane 
Gas (CMG).
How It Works:
Effluent water generated from bagasse 
processing, rich in organic matter, is 
channelled into the biomethanation plant.
 Through a controlled anaerobic 
digestion process, the organic 
content is broken down, producing 
biogas with a high methane 
concentration.Advancing Circular Economy through Bio-methanation for 
Clean Energy 
 This biogas is further purified and 
compressed into Compressed Methane 
Gas (CMG), which serves as a renewable 
substitute for Liquefied Petroleum Gas 
(LPG) and partially offsets coal usage in 
steam generation.
 As an additional benefit, the process also 
yields sodium sulphate as a by-product, 
which is effectively repurposed as a 
make-up chemical in the recovery plant, 
supporting the Company’s closed-loop 
chemical management strategy.
Outcomes and Impact:
 387.44 MT of CMG generated on-
site during FY 2024–25, equivalent 
to 17,994 GJ of renewable energy 
consumption.
 Reduced reliance on external fossil fuels, 
directly lowering operational carbon 
emissions. Enabled partial replacement of LPG and 
coal, contributing to significant cost 
savings and avoided GHG emissions.
 Strengthened internal renewable energy 
generation, supporting ABREL’s long-
term decarbonisation and Net Zero 
goals.
 Reinforced resource circularity by 
transforming wastewater into both 
a renewable energy source and a 
valuable industrial by-product.
This initiative represents a successful 
integration of waste management and 
renewable energy generation, reducing 
our environmental footprint while 
delivering tangible business benefits. 
The bio-methanation plant continues 
to serve as a model for sustainable 
manufacturing within the pulp & paper 
industry, exemplifying our commitment to 
responsible resource utilisation and climate 
action.

Objective
To reduce power consumption, enhance 
air compression capacity, improve 
pressure stability, and ensure overall 
system reliability throughout the plant.
Background and Initiative 
Overview
Compressed air is a critical utility in 
ABREL’s manufacturing operations, 
directly influencing process efficiency 
and energy consumption. Recognising 
inefficiencies in the existing system, 
where two centrifugal compressors 
operated simultaneously, the Company 
undertook a strategic upgrade to install 
a new, high-efficiency centrifugal air 
compressor. The new configuration 
operates with one modern centrifugal 
compressor alongside an existing screw 
compressor, optimising both energy use 
and air supply reliability.Enhancing Energy Efficiency through New Air Compressor 
Installation
Methodology and 
Implementation
 Transitioned from dual centrifugal 
compressors to a hybrid system 
using one advanced centrifugal 
compressor and one screw 
compressor.
 System air pressure was increased 
from 4.9 bar to 5.5 bar, leading to 
improved operational stability.
 Continuous monitoring and 
optimisation ensured the system 
ran efficiently under varying load 
conditions, reducing wear and tear 
on equipment.
Benefits Realised
 Daily Energy Savings: Achieved a 
significant reduction of 4,000 kWh 
per day in power consumption.
 Enhanced Process Stability: Stable 
air pressure improved the reliability 
of plant operations and reduced the frequency of equipment malfunctions.
 Cost Optimisation: Lower energy 
consumption directly translated to 
reduced operational expenses, 
while improved reliability reduced 
maintenance costs.
Outcome
The initiative resulted in a more sustainable 
and cost-efficient air compression system, 
contributing directly to the Company’s 
operational excellence and energy 
conservation objectives. This case 
exemplifies how targeted technological 
upgrades can deliver both environmental 
and economic benefits, aligning with 
ABREL’s commitment to responsible 
manufacturing.

Leveraging Digital Tools for Smarter Construction: Use of 
Maturity Sensors at Birla Niyaara
One major challenge in the real estate sector is efficiently monitoring property conditions and building structures throughout the 
construction process. Traditional methods for testing concrete strength like cube or cylinder testing often present limitations. They are 
labour-intensive, susceptible to handling errors, and reflect only the potential rather than the actual strength under site conditions.
ABREL piloted the use of concrete maturity sensors at Birla Niyaara to improve the accuracy and efficiency of in-place strength assessment. 
By deploying wireless maturity sensors, the Company leveraged a non-destructive, real-time method based on ASTM C1074. These 
sensors continuously capture temperature data to estimate the actual strength development of concrete, offering several advantages:Background
Innovation
Enhanced accuracy 
through uninterrupted real-
time data loggingReliable strength 
prediction based on true 
placement and curing 
conditionsInsights for cost 
optimisation in concrete 
mix design with sufficient 
dataPotential reduction in 
construction cycle times 
through informed, data-
driven decisions
At Birla Niyaara, the design approach balances 
sustainability, comfort, and innovation. As 
part of this commitment, the Company has 
incorporated Low-Emissivity (Low-E) glass into 
the building envelope to enhance energy 
performance and occupant well-being.
Low-E glass features a microscopically 
thin coating that reflects infrared energy 
while allowing visible light to pass through. 
This advanced material supports multiple 
dimensions of performance:
 Energy Efficiency: Reduces heat loss 
in winter and limits solar heat gain in 
summer, lowering reliance on artificial 
heating and cooling systems. Thermal Comfort: Helps maintain stable 
indoor temperatures, minimising cold 
spots and heat build-up near windows.
 UV Protection: Blocks up to 99% of 
harmful UV rays, protecting interiors 
from fading and reducing health risks 
related to prolonged UV exposure.
 Condensation Reduction: Keeps 
interior glass surfaces warmer, thereby 
reducing condensation and the risk of 
mould growth.
 Daylight Harvesting: Allows ample 
natural light while preserving thermal 
insulation, reducing dependence on 
artificial lighting during daytime hours. Environmental Impact: Supports 
reduced energy consumption and 
carbon emissions, contributing to the 
development’s overall sustainability 
goals.
 Aesthetic Value: Offers high visible 
light transmission and is available in 
finishes that suit modern architectural 
aesthetics.
The use of Low-E glass at Birla Niyaara 
demonstrates how material innovation, 
guided by the LifeDesigned® philosophy, 
can transform living spaces while meeting 
the highest standards of environmental 
stewardship and user experience.Integrating Low-E Glass for Sustainable and Comfortable Living at Birla NiyaaraTo build confidence in this approach, maturity sensors were installed at two locations in M80-grade concrete alongside standard strength 
testing through cast cylinders. The results validated the sensors’ reliability and reinforced ABREL’s belief in integrating smart technologies for 
better construction outcomes.

Empowering the Workforce
The Company is deeply committed to empowering its employees, understanding that they are the key drivers of its achievements. ABREL’s progressive 
approach to talent management fosters a supportive and dynamic work environment where employees are equipped and encouraged to thrive, 
innovate, and realise their full potential. 
By implementing comprehensive development programmes and fostering a culture of continuous learning, the Company aims to nurture talent that 
exceeds industry standards. This commitment also ensures that ABREL’s workforce is not only skilled and motivated but also prepared to navigate 
future challenges and drive sustained success for both themselves and the Company.
In FY 2024–25, the Company introduced a 
comprehensive talent management process 
aimed at identifying and nurturing high-
potential employees. This initiative opens 
numerous opportunities for its workforce, 
helping them understand their potential and 
creating pathways for career growth. The 
process includes:Talent Management: A Strategic Approach
Nurturing High-Potential 
Employees
At ABREL, ABG’s talent management 
process is central to nurturing high-potential 
employees. This comprehensive framework 
is designed to identify, assess, and cultivate 
the capabilities of the Company’s workforce, 
aligning their career aspirations with 
organisational objectives.
Potential Assessments: 
Evaluating Future Leaders
The Company is committed to nurturing 
leadership potential across its workforce 
through targeted programmes designed 
to develop essential skills and capabilities. 
These initiatives are tailored to prepare 
the employees for future challenges, 
empowering them to drive the Company's 
strategic objectives with innovation 
and confidence. ABREL’s programmes 
include experiential learning, mentorship 
opportunities, and leadership workshops that are continuously updated to reflect 
industry best practices and emerging 
trends.
In a strategic endeavour to identify and 
nurture future leaders, the potential 
assessment was conducted for 162 
eligible employees, spanning various 
business segments and the head office. 
This comprehensive evaluation used 
ABG’s competencies as the foundational 
framework, meticulously examining 
crucial attributes of aspiration, agility, and 
ability. Through this rigorous process, 
managers and skip-level managers gain 
valuable insights into employees who 
demonstrate a significant potential to drive 
the organisation's growth and lead with 
distinction in their respective roles.
Talent Councils: 
Collaborative Evaluation
Following the execution of the potential 
assessment, the Company established 8 
talent councils, which are composed of 
senior management and cross-functional 
leaders. These councils engage in 
methodical discussions regarding the 
developmental trajectories of over 120 
employees, ensuring evaluations remain 
impartial and comprehensive. 
Through these deliberations, the Company 
derives actionable insights that enhance 
the understanding of employees’ current 
capabilities and their future development 
needs. This strategic approach helps the Company build a robust pipeline 
of skilled leaders, thereby aligning with 
its commitment to fostering leadership 
excellence and organisational growth.

Centre (DAC) Journey:

Employees participate in a meticulously

allows participants to thoroughly assess

prospective roles within the organisation. 
Furthermore, the DAC journey serves as 
an essential tool for tailoring development 
plans to align with individual competencies 
and aspirations. This ensures employees 
realise their full potential and contribute 
strategically to the organisation's success.

Employee Satisfaction at ABREL
ABREL is proud to have launched Vibes, a 
cutting-edge employee satisfaction survey 
designed to assess multiple dimensions of 
its organisational climate. This innovative 
tool is structured around three core themes: 
engagement, business, and workplace, 
each intricately crafted to mirror the 
Company’s operational excellence and 
strategic priorities.
Engagement
The Vibes survey explores key factors 
influencing employees’ motivation, job 
satisfaction, and commitment to the 
Company. By examining aspects such 
as career advancement opportunities, 
recognition and rewards, and alignment 
with Company values and goals, Vibes 
seeks to uncover insights that drive 
enthusiasm and dedication among ABREL’s 
workforce.Business Strategy
Under its business theme, Vibes addresses 
elements related to ABREL's broader 
strategic framework and operational 
dynamics. This includes evaluating 
organisational communication effectiveness, 
clarity of goals, and leadership 
performance. By focussing on these critical 
areas, the survey enables the Company to 
understand how well its strategic vision is 
communicated and perceived across levels.
Workplace Environment
The survey’s workplace theme delves into 
the physical and cultural dimensions of 
the Company’s work setting. It investigates 
factors like workplace safety, inclusivity and 
diversity, and the adequacy of resources 
and support available for optimal employee 
performance. These insights help ABREL ensure an environment that nurtures 
productivity and well-being.
By dissecting each theme into relevant 
categories with precise questions, Vibes 
delivers valuable data that highlights 
the Company’s strengths and identifies 
areas for enhancement. This thorough 
approach facilitates a robust understanding 
of employees' needs and perspectives, 
empowering ABREL to foster a more 
engaging, productive, and supportive 
workplace culture. Consequently, the 
Company is positioned to develop an 
environment that not only meets but 
exceeds the expectations of its valued team 
members.

safe construction environments across the

Identifying Risks and Hazards
ABREL employs consistent practices to diligently identify workplace hazards and conduct ongoing risk assessments across all business sectors. 
This approach includes:
 Behaviour-Based Safety Observation 
(BBSO): This system identifies risks 
linked to unsafe behaviours and 
conditions, improving hazard detection 
and fostering a safer work environment.
 Hazard Identification and Risk 
Assessment (HIRA): This method 
allows the Company to engage with staff, 
assess the working environment, and 
pinpoint potential risks. By proactively 
identifying these risks, ABREL can 
implement effective controls to mitigate 
or eliminate them.
 Regular Safety Audits: Conducted 
by both internal and external entities, 
these audits ensure adherence to safety 
standards and identify potential hazards 
or areas for improvement.
 Job Safety Analysis (JSA): Before 
key activities commence, the Company 
analyses each stage to identify potential 
risks and determine appropriate 
countermeasures. Incident Investigation Mechanism: 
This allows for thorough examination of 
incidents to identify associated risks and 
hazards effectively.

ABREL recognises the importance of active 
worker involvement and consultation in 
advancing occupational health and safety 
(OHS) across all its business verticals. 
Through meaningful engagement, the 
Company empowers the workforce to 
contribute significantly to the creation and 
execution of OHS initiatives, ensuring their 
well-being is consistently prioritised.
Comprehensive SOPs are in place 
to manage work-related hazards and 
incidents. Identified risks are promptly 
addressed, with improvements implemented 
based on thorough assessments. During 
emergencies, occupational health services 
are immediately available to employees, 
with their functionality regularly monitored to 
ensure consistent care and safety.Promoting safety regulation awareness is 
a key priority for ABREL, with structured 
workshops conducted biannually to 
deliver critical briefings to employees,

These workshops are designed to improve

and empower all participants to prioritise 
safety in their daily operations. Moreover,

are well-equipped to uphold the safety 
standards from day one. This proactive 
approach not only enhances compliance 
but also builds a culture of collective 
responsibility and vigilance, contributing 
to a safer and more secure working 
environment for everyone involved.

In the wake of increasing urbanisation and 
evolving agricultural practices, countless 
cows are left neglected and forced to 
wander the streets. Addressing this pressing 
issue, Aditya Birla Group’s initiative at the 
Gaushala in Halduchaur, District Nainital, 
plays a crucial role in providing sustenance 
and care for stray cattle. Through the regular 
provision of cattle feed on a monthly basis,

animals but also offers them a safe haven. 
This compassionate endeavour ensures that 
stray cows have a sanctuary, reflecting the 
Group’s commitment to animal welfare and 
community support.The Gaushala initiative extends far beyond 
the realm of animal care, delivering tangible 
benefits to the local community and 
agricultural sector. By providing shelter for 
stray cattle, the initiative significantly reduces 
the risk of road accidents caused by roaming 
animals, thereby enhancing public safety. 
Furthermore, by preventing stray cattle from 
entering agricultural lands, the Gaushala 
helps protect crops, ensuring that farmers 
do not suffer economic losses. This holistic 
approach exemplifies a model of community 
cooperation, where animal welfare initiatives 
simultaneously bolster agricultural productivity 
and promote harmonious coexistence of 
urban and rural environments.

the design, construction, and operation of its

During the year, this commitment was 
further deepened across both of ABREL’s operating divisions: Real Estate and Pulp 
& Paper, through the advancement of 
initiatives aimed at reducing environmental 
impacts, enhancing resource circularity,

Responsible Consumption and Resource Use
ABREL remains committed to the responsible consumption of materials across both its Real Estate and Pulp & Paper divisions, with a focus on 
minimising reliance on virgin materials, promoting the use of renewable and recycled inputs, and embedding circularity into procurement and design 
practices.
In FY 2024–25, a total of 24,37,109.92 MT of materials were used across both divisions. Of this, 47.07% (11,47,215.25 MT) were sourced from 
renewable materials such as wood, bamboo, bagasse, veneer chips, domestic wastepaper, and imported pulp, primarily within the Pulp & Paper 
operations.
Recycled input materials accounted for 11.75% (2,86,415.38 MT) of ABREL’s total material use, with their application spanning both divisions. In 
the Pulp & Paper operations, recycled inputs included veneer chips, a waste product of the plyboard industry, bagasse from the sugar industry, and 
domestic wastepaper. In the Real Estate projects, recycled materials comprised fly ash, fly ash bricks, ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS), 
and secondary steel.TypeFY 2023–24 FY 2024–25

Assessing Climate Risks to Safeguard 
Natural Capital and Build Resilient Assets
Climate change continues to reshape how organisations engage with the natural environment, 
affecting access to water, energy systems, land use, and broader ecological stability. For a real 
estate business like ABREL that depends on the long-term viability of these resources, climate-
related risks are not distant future concerns; they are immediate design and planning imperatives.
Within ABREL’s Real Estate division, climate risk assessments have become a core component 
of the environmental strategy and sustainability governance framework. These assessments 
help identify potential vulnerabilities in both the built environment and the surrounding natural 
ecosystems, enabling more informed decision-making across site selection, design, material 
use, and operational planning. This insight also supports the preservation and enhancement of 
the natural capital on which the Company depends, while reducing exposure to environmental, 
regulatory, and reputational risks.
ABREL’s assessments address both physical risks such as flooding, heatwaves, water stress, 
and extreme weather events, and transition risks stemming from evolving climate regulations, 
market expectations, and global decarbonisation pathways. In doing so, the Company not only 
strengthens the resilience of its developments but also positions itself to thrive in a low-carbon 
future.In alignment with ABREL’s local sourcing 
policy, the Real Estate operations 
prioritise procurement within a 500 
km radius and continue to substitute 
high-emission materials with circular 
alternatives. Paints and finishing 
materials used across residential and 
commercial assets are restricted to low-
VOC content to minimise environmental 
impact and improve indoor air 
quality. In the Pulp & Paper division, 
wood-based inputs are sourced in 
compliance with Forest Stewardship 
Council® (FSC) guidelines, ensuring 
exclusion of materials from endangered 
or historically sensitive forest areas. 
Additionally, all wood-based materials 
used for finishing in ABREL’s Real Estate 
projects are FSC certified. 
Reclaiming products and packaging at 
end-of-use is not applicable to ABREL 
due to the nature of its operations. 
In the Real Estate business, the 
deliverables consist of permanent 
built assets, including residential and 
commercial developments, which are 
not packaged or movable goods. 
Once delivered, the asset lifecycle is 
managed by homeowners, housing 
societies, or commercial tenants, with 
no associated product packaging to 
reclaim. In the Pulp & Paper division, 
products such as tissue, paper, and 
board are primarily consumed in 
downstream applications where they are 
either biodegradable or integrated into 
secondary manufacturing processes. As 
a result, there is no residual packaging 
or post-consumer material requiring 
end-of-life reclamation, and establishing 
a return system is neither technically 
feasible nor environmentally necessary. 
Given these sector-specific realities, 
reclaiming products or packaging 
is not material to ABREL’s business 
model. Accordingly, the Company’s 
focus remains on responsible sourcing 
and upstream material efficiency, 
while downstream reclamation is not 
considered material due to the nature 
of its products and the sectors in which 
it operates.
Climate risk assessments at ABREL are not solely focussed on 
anticipating future threats; they are also about building smarter, 
more resilient projects in the present.

ABREL’s climate risk assessment framework is designed to be both scientifically robust and operationally relevant. It integrates scenario modelling, 
on-ground risk mapping, and design resilience reviews to ensure that every project, whether upcoming or operational, adheres to high standards of 
climate preparedness.ABREL’s Approach to Climate Risk Assessment and Its Outcome
Physical climate risk assessments at ABREL were conducted using scenario modelling based on 
the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) developed by the IPCC, which represent plausible 
climate futures under different levels of global mitigation.Physical Risk Assessment

Climate risk exposure was assessed across key acute perils (such as flood, wind, and hail) and chronic perils (such as heat, drought, and

Common Risk Trends Identified across ABREL’s Projects
Wind Hazard was identified as a critical acute risk, with multiple assets such as Birla Tisya and Birla Niyaara 
receiving a 'Highest' rating.
Heat Hazard was consistently rated as ‘High’ to ‘Highest’ across all seven projects, with a projected increase 
in the number of days exceeding 35°C by the year 2050.
Precipitation Hazard under SSP5 scenarios also indicated high intensity, with total water-equivalent 
precipitation exceeding 600 mm at certain locations.
Flood Hazard was generally rated as ‘Moderate’ or ‘Low’ , attributed to resilient site topography and the 
presence of built flood defences.
The modelled average annual losses across assets for wind and flood hazards were assessed, while heat-related losses, reflecting lost 
productivity, were also projected to increase across the SSP pathways.I

Transition Risk Assessment
During the fiscal year, ABREL undertook a comprehensive transition risk assessment across its real estate portfolio using the globally recognised 
Carbon Risk Real Estate Monitor (CRREM) framework. This initiative formed part of ongoing efforts to align with the Aditya Birla Group’s Net Zero 
2050 ambition and to future-proof the portfolio against the impacts of a rapidly evolving regulatory, technological, and market landscape.
The transition risk assessment aimed to evaluate how changing climate-related policies, investor expectations, and decarbonisation pathways could 
affect the long-term viability, performance, and valuation of the built assets. The assessment covered all currently owned and recently completed 
commercial and residential assets across key markets, including Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Gurugram.
The objective is to assess how the residential and commercial portfolio aligns with global decarbonisation pathways, 
identify potential stranding risks, and inform long-term planning, investment, and operational strategies.

Early Exposure for Commercial Assets
Commercial assets are expected to encounter transition-related exposure earlier in their lifecycle,

Longer-Term Considerations for Residential Assets

trajectories indicate a need for planned efficiency improvements over the coming decade.

Opportunities and Strategic ResponseAlongside the certification of transition-related risks, the assessment also revealed strategic opportunities that can enhance long-term business 
resilience, operational efficiency, and stakeholder value. Many of these opportunities are already being pursued, strengthening the Company's 
alignment with environmental and economic megatrends. Key opportunities include:
Increased Investment and Deployment of Renewables
Building on the example of Birla Aurora, which now operates on 100% green energy, there is further 
scope to expand renewable energy use across other assets.
Increased Energy Demand and Cost Visibility
The assessment has prompted reviews of long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) and encouraged 
the promotion of green leasing models to manage future energy-related costs and regulatory risks.
Rising Building Standards and Certification Requirements
All assets assessed are either IGBC or LEED-certified, reflecting foundational readiness and market 
differentiation in an increasingly regulated environment.
Insurance and Risk Coverage Improvements
Findings from the assessment are being used to evaluate past insurance claims and ensure vulnerable 
assets are adequately protected through additional cover.
Market Transparency and Consumer Alignment
The Company is strengthening its market intelligence by engaging stakeholders and regularly reviewing 
consumer trends to stay ahead of shifting demand and investor expectations.
Collectively, these assessments enhance the Company’s ability to anticipate physical climate risks, prioritise capital investments, and 
improve long-term asset resilience. By integrating data-driven climate insights into design and planning processes, Birla Estates is 
building a future that is not only sustainable but also adaptive and secure.

To support the energy transition in a measurable way, the Company continues to monitor total 
energy consumption by source and type across both the Real Estate and Pulp & Paper divisions. 
The Real Estate operations primarily depend on electricity sourced from both non-renewable 
grid supplies as well as renewable energy obtained through rooftop solar installations at key 
commercial assets and under-construction sites. During the year, rooftop solar systems were 
operational at Birla Aurora and Birla Centurion, while construction sites such as Birla Vanya and 
Birla Tisya utilised solar-powered lights and sensors to reduce electricity consumption during 
non-peak hours. Diesel and petrol remain the only non-renewable fuels used in the Real Estate 
division, mainly for vehicles and backup generators in commercial buildings and temporary 
infrastructure during early-stage construction where grid power is not yet available. The 
renewable share of energy continues to grow as solar capacity expands across both new and 
existing projects.
The Pulp & Paper division operates with a diverse energy mix, combining electricity and thermal 
fuels to support its large-scale manufacturing operations. Electricity is sourced from the state grid 
as well as on-site solar installations.
In addition to electricity, the division consumes various thermal fuels sourced from both renewable and non-renewable origins. Non-renewable fuels 
include diesel, coal, furnace oil, LPG, and low-sulphur heavy stock (LSHS), which primarily support boilers, drying systems, and other process 
equipment. Renewable fuels constitute a significant portion of the CPP’s energy mix and include black liquor (a by-product of the pulping process),
